name: Marin Brady
life: “I still remember teaching a young tailor to measure a room before a suit.” Sunday often includes a stop at the bank steps, where Marin takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I trained the daughter in tailoring. She told me exactly how little space her first shop needs.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a mustard canvas overshirt and a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. Marin has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Marin rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket during a conversation.
personality: Marin has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Marin can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To price a suitably small first tailoring shop.
family: Anton Roman is Marin’s younger relative by marriage. Marin can always ask for five minutes alone. Anton asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Two names on the chart*, Anton says, “I had to tell a waiting patient why the counter was busy.”
connections: Grey Black. A tenant's actual upstairs neighbor is one of the people measuring how little room a tailor needs. Also in the story is Cassandra Collins (former tailoring pupil).
